Patch series ""Fix hugetlb free path race with memory errors"".
In the discussion of Jiaqi Yan's series ""Improve hugetlbfs read on
HWPOISON hugepages"" the race window was discovered.
https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20230616233447.GB7371@monkey/
Freeing a hugetlb page back to low level memory allocators is performed
in two steps.
1) Under hugetlb lock
column2: remove page from hugetlb lists and clear destructor

column1: 2) Outside lock
column2: allocate vmemmap if necessary and call low level free

column1: Between these two steps
column2: the hugetlb page will appear as a normal

column1: compound page.  However
column2: vmemmap for tail pages could be missing.

column1: If a memory error occurs at this time
column2: we could try to update page

column1: flags non-existant page structs.
A much more detailed description is in the first patch.
The first patch addresses the race window.  However
hugetlb_lock lock/unlock cycle to every vmemmap optimized hugetlb page
free operation.  This could lead to slowdowns if one is freeing a large
number of hugetlb pages.
The second path optimizes the update_and_free_pages_bulk routine to only
take the lock once in bulk operations.
The second patch is technically not a bug fix
and Cc stable to avoid a performance regression.  It can be combined with
the first
column2: but was done separately make reviewing easier.

column1: This patch (of 2):
Freeing a hugetlb page and releasing base pages back to the underlying
allocator such as buddy or cma is performed in two steps:
- remove_hugetlb_folio() is called to remove the folio from hugetlb
lists
column2: get a ref on the page and remove hugetlb destructor.  This

column1: all must be done under the hugetlb lock.  After this call
can be treated as a normal compound page or a collection of base
size pages.
- update_and_free_hugetlb_folio() is called to allocate vmemmap if
needed and the free routine of the underlying allocator is called
on the resulting page.  We can not hold the hugetlb lock here.
One issue with this scheme is that a memory error could occur between
these two steps.  In this case
column2: the memory error handling code treats

column1: the old hugetlb page as a normal compound page or collection of base
pages.  It will then try to SetPageHWPoison(page) on the page with an
error.  If the page with error is a tail page without vmemmap
error will occur when trying to set the flag.
Address this issue by modifying remove_hugetlb_folio() and
update_and_free_hugetlb_folio() such that the hugetlb destructor is not
cleared until after allocating vmemmap.  Since clearing the destructor
requires holding the hugetlb lock
remove_hugetlb_folio() if the vmemmap is present.  This saves a
lock/unlock cycle.  Otherwise
update_and_free_hugetlb_folio() after allocating vmemmap.
Note that this will leave hugetlb pages in a state where they are marked
free (by hugetlb specific page flag) and have a ref count.  This is not
a normal state.  The only code that would notice is the memory error
code
column2: and it is set up to retry in such a case.

column1: A subsequent patch will create a routine to do bulk processing of
vmemmap allocation.  This will eliminate a lock/unlock cycle for each
hugetlb page in the case where we are freeing a large number of pages.
